definition: A digital identity system where users control their own identity data without relying on centralized authorities like governments or corporations to verify and manage it.
metaDescription: Learn about decentralized identity - a system where you control your own digital identity without relying on centralized authorities or corporations.
simpleExplanation: Think of it like having your own personal ID wallet that you control completely. Instead of Facebook or Google managing your online identity, you store and share your credentials yourself, deciding exactly what information to reveal to whom.
whyItMatters: Decentralized identity gives you complete control over your personal data, reduces privacy risks from data breaches at large companies, and prevents identity theft. It eliminates the need to trust corporations with your sensitive information.
technicalDetail: Uses blockchain technology and cryptographic proofs to create tamper-resistant digital credentials. Users store identity data in digital wallets and can selectively disclose verified information without revealing unnecessary details, using standards like DIDs (Decentralized Identifiers) and verifiable credentials.

examples.explanation: You store a cryptographically-signed driver's license in your phone wallet. When buying alcohol, you can prove you're over 21 without revealing your exact birthdate, address, or license number.
Your university issues you a verifiable diploma stored in your digital wallet. You can prove your degree to employers without the employer needing to contact the university directly.
Instead of using 'Login with Facebook,' you authenticate using your decentralized identity, keeping your social media activity separate from other online services.
